scoring_rules: Every behavior score must cite at least one verbatim quote from the transcript, with its timestamp.
If no quote in the transcript supports a judgement, set behavior_pct to null and return an empty evidence array. Do not guess.
Quotes must be copied character-for-character from the transcript. Never paraphrase. Never invent a line that was not said.
verdict must be one of the values in 'verdicts'. tactic must be one of the values in 'tactics'.
Score only what the user did. Absence of a behavior is compliance, not a missing score.

behaviors.name: urgency_resistance
behaviors.label: Urgency Resistance
behaviors.definition: Did the user slow the call down, or match the caller's pace?
behaviors.resisted: Explicitly refuses to act inside the caller's time window, says they will take their time, or names the urgency itself as suspicious.
behaviors.partial: Notices the pressure and stays calm, but keeps engaging on the caller's timeline without pushing back on it.
behaviors.complied: Speeds up, apologises for delays, asks what to do quickly, or agrees to act before the stated deadline.
behaviors.evidence_hint: Look at what the user says in the 15 seconds after the caller first mentions a deadline.

behaviors.name: independent_verification
behaviors.label: Independent Verification
behaviors.definition: Did the user end the call and dial a number they sourced themselves?
behaviors.resisted: States they will hang up and call the bank on a number from their card, app, or statement — and then actually disengages.
behaviors.partial: Demands the caller prove identity, or asks for a callback number, but never sources a number independently.
behaviors.complied: Never raises verification, or accepts the caller's own proof such as a case number or a number the caller reads out.
behaviors.evidence_hint: A callback number supplied by the caller is NOT verification. That is the scam. Score it as complied.

behaviors.name: information_withholding
behaviors.label: Information Withholding
behaviors.definition: Did the user confirm any identifying detail?
behaviors.resisted: Declines to confirm anything, including details the caller appears to already know.
behaviors.partial: Confirms only non-identifying facts, such as that they are a customer or that they can talk right now.
behaviors.complied: Confirms or supplies account digits, address, date of birth, a one-time code, or a balance.
behaviors.evidence_hint: Confirming a detail the caller already stated still counts as complied. The confirmation is the attack — it tells the scammer the data is correct.

behaviors.name: authority_deference
behaviors.label: Authority Deference
behaviors.definition: Did the user treat the caller's institutional framing as proof of identity?
behaviors.resisted: Points out that anyone can claim to be from a bank, questions the case number, or notes that banks do not call and ask for this.
behaviors.partial: Voices doubt about who the caller is, but cooperates anyway.
behaviors.complied: Accepts claims like 'our systems flagged this automatically', uses deferential or apologetic language, or follows instructions because the caller sounds official.
behaviors.evidence_hint: Listen for the user apologising, thanking the caller, or saying 'sorry' — deference usually shows up as politeness.
